research.instruction: Collect source-linked business facts and source conversion intent. Return uncertainties, not invented proof. No implementation edits.

brand.instruction: Extract actual rendered fonts, source brand identity and asset provenance using existing helpers. Do not design the page before copy acceptance.

copy.instruction: Own the complete conversion argument, evidence-backed advantage and copy master. Perform the existing editorial acceptance procedure before layout; do not create new human approval requirements.

assets.instruction: Source, prepare and review purposeful imagery. Use scripts for derivatives. Preserve independent-original lineage and distinguish illustration from proof. Use only image tools actually available; no API-key dependency.

frontend.instruction: Implement the frozen production contract. Preserve exact copy, CTA semantics, source conversion intent, responsive imagery and accessible form states. Never hide required content to pass a measurement.

pdf.instruction: Produce and render the useful PDF from the frozen copy and claims. Inspect every page. Keep owner/QA narration out of buyer content. Do not generate unsupported prices or promises.

integration.instruction: Integrate only selected modules. Reuse the maintained backend and identity verifier. Customize configuration, not authentication/storage/attribution internals. No live writes, DNS changes, paid services or deployment.

review.instruction: Independently inspect current actual page/PDF pixels, source evidence and functional results. Do not trust builder pass booleans. Return precise findings and retest requirements. Do not edit product files or approve publication.

debug.instruction: Resolve a bounded high-impact or cross-component failure from its task packet, relevant source and failed tests. Preserve public contracts and existing guards. Return the smallest evidenced repair.

mechanical.instruction: Run an existing deterministic helper. The coordinator executes it directly; no model call is required for the operation.
